Parallel output changes only complete-line ordering between the two logs for each ABI; their line multisets match exactly, and every log independently satisfies the exact fail-closed Cap32 proof.

The pristine source is commit 4abfb8be233bec630f369379fb6c1d92d31f1c7d, tree c9704612f7acd0459125bc28427212def1cce681, with no submodules. The proof binds native leading-space version 4abfb8b to all 44 C compile commands per ABI, every source/object and ordered compiler invocation, the Makefile lines 485 and 511 traces, the exact ordered link, zero warnings or notes, and binary identity 4.5.4 4abfb8b HI.

Resolver metadata advertises display_version v4.2.0 while the built binary identifies 4.5.4 4abfb8b HI. That presentation mismatch remains a target-integration gate and is not sanitized by rewriting upstream metadata.

Resolver metadata labels the core GPLv2, but compiled libretro integration source includes additional non-commercial redistribution terms. The package carries neither corresponding source nor a license inventory, so any public distribution or release remains a human legal and policy gate even though the local bytes reproduce.

Both builds clone the exact source over the network; no offline source bundle or network-disabled rebuild is proven. The portable toolchain archives and loaded image identities are locked, but cached images retain dockerfile_linkage=unverified-local-cache as an explicit provenance limitation.

CPC and GX4000 content loading, disk and tape handling, playlists, keyboard and mouse focus, controls, audio and video pacing, saves, states, frontend integration, compatibility, and sustained performance remain target-runtime gates. Static build evidence establishes no device eligibility.

ARM64 reaches GLIBC_2.29 and records the AArch64 loader, libc, and libm; ARMHF is EABI5 hard-float, requires GLIBC_2.4, libc, and libm. Provider compatibility is unverified. The portable artifacts bind only to ra64-universal-v1 and ra32-a30-v1; all device views remain ineligible pending provider and target-runtime evidence.
